title: Modular tool loop harness with progressive sanitizers and recursion sentinels
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
The current tool execution loop has grown organically to support streaming outputs, function/tool calling, and structured JSON results. In production workloads we see two recurring failure classes: 1) inadvertent infinite or deep recursion when models re-invoke the same tool(s) with near-identical context, and 2) unsafe or malformed tool results that, when injected back into the input for downstream tools or the model, surface PII, control characters, or schema drift.

Goal:
Design and implement a modular "tool loop harness" that: (a) supports multi-tool chaining with streaming partial-results, (b) performs progressive sanitization and schema normalization on tool outputs before injection, (c) enforces recursion/loop guards and idempotency checks, and (d) provides a compatibility layer that adapts legacy tool result shapes into the new structured output contract without forcing all tools to be updated simultaneously. The harness must integrate with the runtime's KV/prefix cache and preserve our low-latency streaming guarantees for hosted and dedicated deployments.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Include: core runtime guards, sanitizer pipeline stages (sanitizer plugins), recursion detector, backward-compatible adapter layer, telemetry hooks, unit/integration tests, and docs.
- Exclude: rewriting third-party tools; we will provide adapters and opt-in progressive rollouts.

Design highlights:
1) Progressive sanitizer pipeline: a sequence of lightweight stages applied in order (trim control chars, enforce UTF-8 normalization, redaction rules for known PII patterns, structured-schema validator, and final token-safety filter). Each stage emits a deterministic "sanitizer fingerprint" attached to the tool-call metadata so we can reason about cache validity and debugging.
2) Streaming-aware injection: when a tool streams partial structured output (e.g., incremental JSON chunks or newline-delimited objects), the harness buffers at safe cutpoints (schema boundaries) instead of waiting for the full response whenever possible. Partial injections may be permitted when downstream tools accept incremental updates via the new stream-compatible call contract.
3) Recursion sentinel & loop detector: maintain a short-lived ring buffer of recent tool-call fingerprints per request (tool_id + input-signature + sanitized-output-fingerprint). If the same fingerprint appears more than N times within T seconds or the call-stack depth exceeds a configured threshold, the harness will: a) short-circuit further calls with a structured fallback result, b) surface an explicit "recursion_detected" status to the orchestrator and metrics, and c) optionally attempt a safe alternative (switch to a sibling tool variant or a read-only cached result).
4) Compatibility bridge: a per-tool adapter map that converts legacy string/blobby outputs into the structured fields the harness expects using declarative transforms (regex extraction, JSON heuristics, CSV -> object mapper). Adapters run before the sanitizer pipeline. The bridge supports hot-reloadable adapter rules so Ops can ship fixes without rolling code.
5) Cache and idempotency integration: sanitized fingerprints are used as cache keys for prefix/KV caching. The harness ensures that sanitizer or adapter changes invalidate or annotate cached entries to avoid silent regressions.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Unit + integration tests cover chaining of >=3 tools with streaming partial outputs and adapters.
- Recursion guard triggers in synthetics for intentionally looping prompts and prevents >95% of runaway token costs in those tests.
- False-positive rate for sanitizer redaction <1% on internal corpora (measured by eval harness).
- No end-to-end median latency regression >5% for 95th percentile streaming flows on Dedicated staging cluster.
- Playground/Console shows sanitizer fingerprints and recursion events in the call-level timeline.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-eager sanitization may alter semantics and break downstream logic. Mitigation: progressive, opt-in sanitizer levels and an "allowlist" mode for trusted tools.
- Risk: Compatibility rules become a maintenance tax. Mitigation: provide tooling to author & test adapter rules and host a small library of common adapters.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec sanitizer pipeline and fingerprint format (doc + examples).
2) Implement lightweight sanitizer stages and unit tests.
3) Add adapter bridge with sample adapters for 3 canonical tools.
4) Implement ring-buffer recursion detector and short-circuit behavior.
5) Hook into streaming path and ensure schema-boundary buffering is robust.
6) Add cache-key integration and invalidation hooks.
7) End-to-end tests, load tests, and console/telemetry integration.

Open questions:
- Exact default thresholds for recursion (N, T) across small/medium/large models. Proposed defaults: N=2 repeats within T=10s, max depth=6. Need experimentation.
- Whether adapters should be authored in a domain-specific language (DSL) or JSON-based rule set.
